svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.10 FIRE PROTECTION
Penetrations by Outlet Boxes or Service Equipment in Concealed Spaces

g.text: Box sealed by a firestop with an FT rating not

(100.8 in²) per 9.3 m² (100 ft²), gap not over 3 mm (⅛″)
Sentences (1) and (2): boxes in a rated face
not over 0.3 m² (3.2 ft²), closing four sides and the back

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Outlet boxes may penetrate the membrane of a rated assembly if sealed by
a firestop with an FT rating not less than the rating of the fire
separation
CAN/ULC-S115. Except as in Sentences (2) to (5). See Note A-9.10.9.8.(1).
Noncombustible outlet boxes in a fire separation or rated membrane need
not meet (1) if
(a) each is not over 0.016 m² (24.8 in²) and they total not over 0.065 m² (100.8
in²) in any 9.3 m² (100 ft²) of surface, and (b) the annular space is not over 3
mm (⅛″). Except as in Sentence 9.10.9.6.(2).
Combustible outlet boxes in a fire separation or rated membrane need not
meet (1) if
(a) they are (i) closed off from the rest of the assembly space by fire block
material to Article 9.10.16.3. in an enclosure not over 0.3 m² (3.2 ft²), or
(ii) in a space filled with rock or slag fibre insulation (CAN/ULC-S702.1) of at
least 1.22 kg/m² (0.25 lb/ft²) of wall surface that encapsulates their exposed
sides and back, and (b) they total not over 0.016 m² (24.8 in²) per enclosure or
insulated space. Except as in Sentence 9.10.9.6.(2).
Noncombustible boxes to (2) may be on opposite sides of a rated vertical
fire separation without meeting (1) if they are
(a) at least 600 mm (23⅝″) apart horizontally, (b) enclosed as in Subclause
(3)(a)(i), or (c) in an insulated space as in Subclause (3)(a)(ii).
Combustible boxes to (3) may be on opposite sides of a rated vertical
fire separation without meeting (1)
Service equipment may penetrate a horizontal fire separation conforming
to Sentence 9.10.9.12.(2) if the penetration is sealed by
(a) a firestop with an FT rating not less than the required rating
(CAN/ULC-S115), or a firestop to Clause 9.10.9.6.(1)(a) where (b) the equipment
is entirely within a wall cavity above and below, or (c) the penetration is (i)
in the concealed space of a rated floor or ceiling, (ii) above a ceiling
membrane providing a horizontal fire separation, or (iii) in a horizontal
service space to Sentence 9.10.9.12.(2) directly above or below a floor or
ceiling.
Larger boxes need no firestop under (1) if set in a recessed enclosure that
keeps the rating continuous. Enclosure material should span the framing so all
four sides and the back of the box are enclosed. Wiring through an enclosure
must meet all applicable requirements.
Drawn: close-ups of stud walls and a rated ceiling, some boards left off to show the cavity. Orange: firestop. Blue: combustible box. Box sizes are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.10.9.8. (page 9-68)
